clue.text: Taking money out for retirement

definitions.meaning: removing cash from a bank account is making a bank transaction of this kind
a retreat or pulling back from a position or from public life

explanation.surface: Someone draws on their savings to fund life after work.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share the idea of drawing back: cash drawn from an account, and a person drawing back from the world.

clue.text: Counsel is exhausted, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for exhausted is spoken and a same-sounding word entered

parts.note: worn out means exhausted

explanation.surface: A lawyer is tired out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Counsel' looks like a barrister but is a verb here. In non-rhotic British speech WORN and WARN sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To counsel someone can mean to caution or advise them against something.

clue.text: Accept a holiday and say goodbye

parts.note: to accept is to take
leave is time off work, a holiday

explanation.surface: Someone takes a break from work and bids colleagues farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to bid farewell before departing.

clue.text: Father may be cleric within 24 hours

indicators.note: within signals the cleric's letters go inside the word for 24 hours

parts.note: a day lasts 24 hours
DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a degree held by clergy

explanation.surface: A priest might become a father in a single day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father' looks like a priest's title, alongside 'cleric'; it is the familiar word for a parent.
explanation.definitionFit: A childish or affectionate word for one's male parent.

clue.text: Books which one enjoys in bed?

definitions.meaning: yearbooks, such as children's yearly gift books
flowers lasting a single season, enjoyed in a flower bed rather than a bed for sleeping

explanation.surface: Bedtime reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both yearly gift books and plants that complete their life in one year, grown in a flower bed.

clue.text: Lace with gin in a way that's divine!

indicators.note: in a way suggests the letters are put in some other arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Spiking a drink with gin is heavenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lace' looks like the verb for spiking a drink, which fits 'gin'; it is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something like an angel is heavenly or divine.

clue.text: Join me as ordered

indicators.note: the words me and as are put into a new order, as if arranged on command

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A plea to sign up, framed as an instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as ordered' signals rearranging ME and AS; the second 'as' is part of the indicator, the first is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A seam is the line where two pieces of fabric are joined, so as a verb it means to join.

clue.text: Demoted at the centre, get all worked up

indicators.note: at the centre picks the middle letters of the word demoted, dropping its ends

explanation.surface: An employee demoted at head office gets upset.
explanation.definitionFit: To display exaggerated feeling, theatrically, is to get worked up.

clue.text: Meticulous employee that comes round on time

parts.note: minute means precise and meticulous
a hand is a worker, as in a farm hand

explanation.surface: A careful worker who always turns up on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes round on time' suggests a punctual visitor; it is a pointer sweeping a clock face.
explanation.definitionFit: The longer pointer on a clock sweeps round the dial, marking time.

clue.text: Reform a crook reportedly put into difficulties

indicators.note: reportedly signals a word that sounds like the phrase meaning reform a crook

parts.note: to straighten out a criminal is to reform them

explanation.surface: A reformed crook ends up in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in straitened circumstances is to be hard up or in difficulty.

clue.text: Had an inclination and worked in the garden

definitions.meaning: sloped, as a stage or a ship's mast slopes at an angle
used a toothed garden tool to gather leaves or level soil

explanation.surface: A gardener felt like gardening and then did some.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake is a slope (a raked stage), and raking is drawing a garden tool over the soil.

clue.text: Willie Winkie's running gear

parts.note: in the nursery rhyme Wee Willie Winkie runs through the town in his bedclothes; 'running gear' sounds like sports kit

explanation.surface: Talk of a nursery-rhyme character's athletic kit.
explanation.walkthrough: Wee Willie Winkie is a Scottish nursery rhyme figure who runs through the town upstairs and downstairs in his nightwear, checking children are in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme dresses its runner in a long sleeping garment, so that is the outfit he runs in.

clue.text: Co-operate in production of drama and dance

parts.note: a drama is a play
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Working together to stage a theatre and dance show.
explanation.definitionFit: To play ball is an idiom for agreeing to work along with someone.

clue.text: Wide awake for a siren call

definitions.meaning: a warning signal sounded by a siren, as in an air-raid warning

explanation.surface: Someone jolted fully awake by a siren.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for watchfulness and a noun for a warning signal such as an air-raid siren.

clue.text: Timely sort of police raid

indicators.note: sort of suggests the letters of police raid are sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: A police raid that arrives at just the right moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Recurring at regular intervals of time, a loose sense of timely.

clue.text: Scholar takes ages, with total backing

parts.note: ages are long periods, eras

indicators.note: backing means the word for total is read backwards

parts.note: a total is a sum

explanation.surface: A slow scholar who keeps a full tally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses the word for total, placed after the ages; 'takes' and 'with' are just joining words.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch Renaissance humanist of Rotterdam was one of the great scholars of his age.

clue.text: A meal oft served out cold? Yes

definitions.text: A meal oft served out cold? Yes

indicators.note: served out suggests the letters of a meal oft are dished up in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Asks whether a dish is usually eaten cold, and confirms it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the dish while 'served out' rearranges A MEAL OFT.
explanation.definitionFit: A loaf of minced meat, often eaten sliced cold, is just such a meal.

clue.text: Stuffy complaint

parts.note: reads like a pompous grievance but means an ailment that blocks the nose

explanation.surface: A pompous, starchy grumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuffy' suggests a prim manner and 'complaint' a grievance; read medically they are a blocked-up illness.
explanation.definitionFit: This is excess mucus in the nose and throat, a condition that leaves one feeling stuffed up.

clue.text: They control ovens, cooking the roasts

indicators.note: cooking implies the letters of the roasts are cooked up into something new

explanation.surface: Oven controls are at work on a roast dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Variable resistors regulate current, as in the dials that set an electric oven's heat.

clue.text: One about to settle in the country

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
re means about or concerning
to land is to come to rest, to settle

explanation.surface: A person thinking of making a home somewhere rural.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the country' looks like countryside but names a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The island republic west of Great Britain is a nation, hence a country.

clue.text: Lot of the French money has variable support

indicators.note: in a down clue the variable supports, so its letter sits below the rest

parts.note: des means of the in French
tin is slang for money
y is a standard algebraic variable

explanation.surface: A French lot of money carries a variable underpinning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lot' looks like a quantity but means one's fate. TIN is old British slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: One's lot in life is one's fate.

clue.text: Business worry

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a commercial firm and a feeling of anxiety.

clue.text: It provides food or water

definitions.meaning: a works or school dining room serving meals
a soldier's or camper's flask for carrying drinking water

explanation.surface: Something that supplies food or drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a staff dining room and a water flask for hikers or soldiers.

clue.text: Peg possibly owed a pound

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters of owed could be arranged another way

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A debt of a pound, perhaps, pegged to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges the word owed; 'a pound' supplies the familiar sterling abbreviation at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden pin used to join two pieces of timber is a kind of peg.

clue.text: West Country lady

parts.note: Oman is a country in Arabia

explanation.surface: A woman from England's West Country, the southwest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West Country' reads as the English region; it splits into W and a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A lady is an adult female person.

clue.text: Direction to take off frock

parts.note: S, for south, is a compass direction
to take off one's clothes is to undress

explanation.surface: An instruction to remove a dress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take off frock' reads as one instruction; 'frock' is actually the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A light summer dress worn in hot weather is a type of frock.

clue.text: Appropriate ceremonial form in speech

indicators.note: in speech signals a word that sounds the same as the ceremony word

parts.note: a rite is a ceremonial form or ritual

explanation.surface: A ritual suited to a formal speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fitting or correct is appropriate.

clue.text: Right conclusion? Tear it up

parts.note: a conclusion is an end

explanation.surface: A decision to rip up a document once it is settled.
explanation.definitionFit: To rend is to tear apart violently.

clue.text: Expect high tolls here

parts.note: sounds like a costly toll road, but tolls are the ringing of bells high up in a tower

explanation.surface: A warning about pricey road charges ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tolls' looks like road charges; here it is the sound of bells ringing in a tall tower.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian word names a free-standing bell tower, where bells ring out high above.

clue.text: Not acute, but quite serious

definitions.meaning: the ... accent is the counterpart of the acute accent in writing

explanation.surface: An illness that is chronic rather than sudden, but still worrying.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the accent opposite to acute, and also an adjective for solemn seriousness.

clue.text: Policy revealed in short note

explanation.surface: A government stance leaked through a brief memo.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an official stance (toe the party line) and a brief written message.

clue.text: Sent off with a wave of the hand?

definitions.text: Sent off with a wave of the hand?

parts.words: Sent off with a wave of the hand?
parts.note: sounds like a dismissive farewell, but describes a hypnotist putting someone into a trance with hand passes

explanation.surface: Someone dismissed with a casual flick of the hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent off' suggests dismissal; read as 'sent off to sleep', it is a trance induced by a hypnotist's gestures.
explanation.definitionFit: A person put into a trance by a mesmerist's hand passes has been sent off into another state.
